resources.string: What choosing, editing, deleting, restoring and updating do to your Layouts, themes and word lists

Appearance, Layout & typing, Text correction, Swipe and the Fine-tune screens hold your changes until you save or leave, with the changed settings in italics. Every other screen saves a change at once.
Appearance, Layout & typing, Text correction and Swipe hold your changes until you save or leave, with the changed settings in italics. Every other screen saves a change at once.
Leaving a screen keeps your changes: on
Back, Save and leaving the app keep your changes without asking. Only Discard asks, and then undoes them. On to start with; the switch is in App settings (advanced).
Leaving a screen keeps your changes: off
Back and Save ask first. Leaving the app, or closing the settings window, undoes the changes you didn\'t save.
The palette editor and Customize popups have their own Save and Discard and always ask, whatever the switch. Leaving the app undoes what you hadn\'t saved there. What you saved stays.
Saved Layouts, themes and popup sets
Changing a setting changes this keyboard only, shown as \"Custom · from Sunset\". The saved item changes only with its save icon in the list.

With separate settings on, a change stays on the keyboard you\'re editing. Off, every keyboard uses the first keyboard\'s settings, so a change reaches all of them. Backup, restore, app update and factory reset each have their own column below.
Puts all its settings and keys on this keyboard. The built-in Layouts always follow the latest defaults.
Puts its colors, fonts, pictures and look on this keyboard.
Puts its popups, accents, symbol map and popup order on this keyboard.
This keyboard\'s light or dark colors. One list of palettes for every keyboard; a saved theme names its palettes, it holds no copy.
This keyboard\'s font for that text.
This keyboard\'s keys for that kind of layout.

A saved item\'s settings that were at their default when saved: with \"Saved items take new defaults\" on they take today\'s defaults, off they apply as saved. Flipping the switch changes the keyboards using them at once, switched-off ones too; if a popup set\'s accents would make two keyboards the same, you\'re asked first, and OK gives the lower one the next number. With it off, a setting still at the value the keyboard\'s chosen item kept for its default is saved at its default again (the save icon, Save as new).

Changes stay on this keyboard, shown as \"Custom · from Sunset\". The saved item changes only with its save icon in the list, which asks which other keyboards using it get the change. Everything waits for the screen\'s Save, or for leaving the screen while \"Leaving a screen keeps your changes\" is on; Discard undoes it everywhere.

Key edits stay on this keyboard, as for Layouts and themes; the set changes only with its save icon. Saved Layouts holding the set are listed with ticks too. Customize popups always asks before you leave it, and leaving the app undoes what it hadn\'t saved.

Edited in the palette editor: every keyboard and saved theme using it changes. If others use it, its Save asks for each, switched-off keyboards too: the new colors, the default ones, or the old ones kept as the next number, \"Warm 2\", one for all that keep them. Discard there, or on Appearance, undoes it all. Leaving the app undoes what the editor hadn\'t saved, whatever the switch.
Edits the layout file: every keyboard using it changes. Layout & Typing\'s Discard undoes it.
With separate settings, each keyboard\'s settings are its own; with one set of settings (the first keyboard\'s), a change reaches every keyboard.
Saves this keyboard\'s settings under a new name. If another saved item has exactly these settings, the dialog says so; it still saves.
Long-press the name. Every keyboard and saved item naming it follows. Waits for the screen\'s Save.
In the palette editor. Every keyboard and saved theme naming it follows.
Keyboards and saved Layouts using it follow.
Off the list only. Keyboards using it keep its settings, shown as Custom; nothing goes back to the default. The dialog names them. Waits for the screen\'s Save.
Off the list. Keyboards using it keep its popups as Custom; saved Layouts keep its popups without the name, and it never comes back by itself.

One nothing else uses is deleted. Else you choose: all to default (every keyboard and saved theme using it goes to the default colors, and it leaves the list), or only this keyboard (it goes to the default colors, the others keep the palette). Appearance\'s Discard undoes it.
The file goes. Every keyboard and saved theme using it goes back to the default font; you\'re asked first, and the question names them, or says nothing uses it. Waits for the screen\'s Save.
Off the picture list; keyboards and themes keep their copies.
Off the list. Every keyboard using it keeps its keys as an unsaved layout of its own, whether it chose it or had it as the default for that part.
Its learned and blacklisted words go too. Keyboards reading them (\"Use lists from other keyboards\") are named, and one you pick can take them, merged into its own.

One no keyboard uses is deleted. One in use: if only this keyboard uses it and the language has another version, \"Replace with … and delete this one\" does both; otherwise select another version for the keyboards using it first. A language\'s only dictionary can\'t be deleted while a keyboard uses the language.
Delete in the Learned list: gone as if never typed, also for keyboards reading this list.
Delete in the Blacklisted list: the word can be suggested again.
Remove (long-press a suggestion) deletes it there too, with the learned word, and blacklists it on this keyboard.
Unpin or delete it in the clipboard: one list for every keyboard.
A setting\'s Default button: this keyboard only. It then follows the latest default.
Choosing the Layout, theme or popup set again brings back what it carries.
Add a palette, or Load one from a file or text.
Load a font file in a text style. The same font loaded again is reused.
Pick a picture: it joins the picture list every keyboard chooses from.
Add custom layout (paste one into the editor), or Load file in Full customization with JSON.
Add a keyboard, or a copy of one. It gets its own settings at once, from the ones you pick. A new keyboard can start with words from other keyboards.
Add from Downloads, or get one from curmudgeon.works.
Add word, in Android\'s personal dictionary.
Save the palette to a file, or copy it as text, in the palette editor.
A backup holds everything but the logs: swipe results, swipe corpus, corrections and settings changes (Backup and restore).
Included as they are, with the values their unpicked settings had when saved.
Each keyboard\'s settings: only what you picked.
Fonts, pictures, custom key layouts and added dictionaries are included.
Learned and blacklisted words, Android\'s personal dictionary and the clipboard are included.

Untick \"Full restore (delete app data)\" and choose keyboards (all ticked to start with): one whose language no keyboard on this device has is marked new and comes in added. For one whose language this device has, switched-off keyboards included, you\'re asked first: merge it into one of those keyboards (one only, nothing picked for you), or keep it as a separate keyboard. Merging lists only what differs (each part of the keyboard, each menu whose settings differ; its learned and blacklisted words, ticked to start with): a ticked item takes the backup\'s, an unticked one keeps this device\'s, and nothing ticked restores nothing of it. Merged, the name box starts with the keyboard\'s current name; kept separate, a name another keyboard has gets the next number (counting up one it ends with). Ticked menus that are common to all your keyboards (App settings › Separate settings per keyboard) are named there: restored into the first keyboard, every keyboard shows them; into another, they wait in its own settings, and a dialog after the restore says so.

Come in without asking unless the same one (name and content) is here already. One that clashes with yours is listed under \"For other clashes\", ticked to start with. Same name, other content: ticked, the backup\'s takes the name and yours gets the next free number, \"Sunset 2\"; every keyboard and saved item using \"Sunset\" then uses the backup\'s. Unticked, the backup\'s doesn\'t come in, and the restored keyboards that chose it use yours. The same content under another name: ticked, yours is renamed to the backup\'s name everywhere; unticked, nothing is renamed and the restored keyboards use yours. A built-in name stays the built-in\'s: the backup\'s gets the next number. A Layout\'s popup set is matched first, and the keyboards point at what their items became.

Come in like the saved items, compared by their colors, ticked to start with: a palette with your palette\'s name and other colors takes the name, yours becomes \"Warm 2\", and every keyboard and saved theme on \"Warm\" takes the backup\'s colors; one with your palette\'s colors under another name renames yours everywhere. Unticked, nothing of yours changes.

The restored keyboards\' files: the same file here already is used; a name in use for another file gets the next free number, \"Mine 2\", and the restored keyboards, themes (fonts, pictures) and Layouts (key layouts) name that one; this device\'s file is never replaced. A restored Layout\'s own custom key layouts come in too: under their names, or, with other keys under a name you use, as its tick says: ticked, the Layout\'s keys take the name and yours gets the next number, \"My numrow 2\", with every keyboard and Layout using it following; unticked, the Layout keeps its keys as its own copy.

Each restored keyboard brings its learned words: they\'re added to this device\'s, never replacing them, and a word on both keeps the higher count, so restoring twice changes nothing. \"Android personal dictionary words\" (under \"Also restore\", ticked to start with) adds the backup\'s words of Android\'s personal dictionary that this device lacks.

Each restored keyboard brings the dictionaries of its languages, no tick: the same one here already, nothing changes; a new one comes in; one that differs from yours comes in and is selected, and yours is kept aside as \"…prev\", still selectable. \"Other dictionaries\" (under \"Also restore\", ticked to start with) brings the backup\'s dictionaries no restored keyboard brings.

\"Clipboard history\" (under \"Also restore\", ticked to start with) merges: the backup\'s clips are added, a clip on both stays once, both sides\' pins are kept, newest first, and the history size drops the oldest unpinned ones.
The device\'s \"Saved items take new defaults\" switch stays as it is.

Wipes this device\'s settings and replaces them with the backup\'s: keyboards, saved items, files, word lists, dictionaries and clipboard. Android\'s personal dictionary is merged: the backup\'s words are added. A clipboard the backup can\'t read is skipped, and this device\'s clips stay. The device\'s \"Saved items take new defaults\" switch stays as it is.
What you picked stays; what you never picked follows the new defaults.

With \"Saved items take new defaults\" on, the keyboards using a saved item take the new defaults for the settings it saved at their default; off, the update changes no keyboard. Built-ins always follow.
Every setting back to its default. Nothing ticked: back to the one keyboard of the first start. Ticked \"Keyboards and languages\": the keyboards and their languages stay.

Go, unless \"Saved layouts & popups …\" is ticked. Ticked with the keyboards, each keyboard also keeps its popups, key layouts, pictures, palettes and fonts, and its chosen Layout, popup set and theme are applied again (changes made on top of them are undone). \"Saved items take new defaults\" is kept only when that box is ticked; otherwise it goes back on.
Go, unless ticked. Words kept but not the keyboards: the removed keyboards\' learned and blacklisted words join the default keyboard\'s, every script.
On: each keyboard uses its own settings, as it left them. Nothing is copied; a keyboard added has its own from the start.

Off: every keyboard uses the first keyboard\'s settings (the first in the list), and a change from any keyboard changes them. Each keyboard\'s own settings stay stored and come back when it\'s on again. A menu shared under Separate settings per keyboard works the same way.
The first keyboard can\'t be deleted while its settings are the common ones (separate settings off, or a menu shared): move another keyboard to the top first.
Moving another keyboard to the top makes its settings the common ones, at once.
Saved items are shared by all keyboards either way. With one set of settings, the update and delete dialogs have no keyboards to tick.
Each keyboard always keeps its own learned and blacklisted words.
